_comment: WMS side of the storefront promise (cmd/seed-storefront, WMS step). The CPT (critical pull time) schedule of the storefront's fulfilment site in process-path-management (PUT /sites/{id}/cpt-schedule), written under TWO ids from this one list of cutoffs. siteId is the NETWORK's id of the building (the node's vendorNodeCode and network-fulfillment's SITE_ID, site-1): network-fulfillment caps every listing's advertised quantity at the process-path capacity before this site's NEXT cutoff, and the network declares the same node with the cutoffs and timezone of warehouse-infra scripts/data/retail-network-seed.json (fulfillmentNodes[vendorNodeCode=site-1].profile): the two MUST agree (fixture_test.go and the seeder's CHECK enforce it). warehouseSiteId is the facility-layout site of the warehouse building that serves that node (ADR 0001 D1, e2e-tests docs/storefront-provisioning.md): network-fulfillment maps site-1 to it (NETWORK_SITE_MAP) and sends it as fulfillmentSiteId, so order-management promises against, and outbound-shipping needs, a schedule under THIS id. It must match ^[A-Z0-9]+$ (order-management, facility-layout and outbound-shipping accept no other site code), must differ from siteId, and must already exist in facility-layout (the seeder checks it and never creates it). CURATED: the cutoff ids, every day of the week, shipMethod ground (the fleet's only method) and the PICK path (the path of customer orders, intake CUSTOMER_ORDER). make warehouse-day never writes either id: it runs on its own site (SIM1) and refuses both siteId and warehouseSiteId (cmd/warehouse-day/site.go) unless -allow-live-site; make provision-storefront restores a schedule that differs.
